name: Python Off-by-One Error
description: A Python function intended to return the last N items from a list. Contains an off-by-one error: uses lst[len(lst)-n+1:] instead of the correct lst[len(lst)-n:] (or equivalently lst[-n:]). When called with n=3 on [1,2,3,4,5], it returns [4,5] instead of [3,4,5].

name: Python Clean Code (Stack Implementation)
code:
from typing import Any, Optional


class StackEmptyError(Exception):
    """Raised when an operation is attempted on an empty stack."""
    pass


class Stack:
    """A last-in, first-out (LIFO) data structure.

    This implementation uses a Python list as the underlying storage.
    All operations (push, pop, peek) run in amortized O(1) time.

    Attributes:
        _items: Internal list storing the stack elements.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initialize an empty stack."""
        self._items: list[Any] = []

    def push(self, item: Any) -> None:
        """Push an item onto the top of the stack.

        Args:
            item: The element to add to the stack.
        """
        self._items.append(item)

    def pop(self) -> Any:
        """Remove and return the top item from the stack.

        Returns:
            The most recently pushed item.

        Raises:
            StackEmptyError: If the stack is empty.
        """
        if self.is_empty():
            raise StackEmptyError("Cannot pop from an empty stack.")
        return self._items.pop()

    def peek(self) -> Any:
        """Return the top item without removing it.

        Returns:
            The most recently pushed item.

        Raises:
            StackEmptyError: If the stack is empty.
        """
        if self.is_empty():
            raise StackEmptyError("Cannot peek at an empty stack.")
        return self._items[-1]

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        """Check whether the stack contains no items.

        Returns:
            True if the stack is empty, False otherwise.
        """
        return len(self._items) == 0

    def size(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of items in the stack.

        Returns:
            The current number of elements.
        """
        return len(self._items)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Return a developer-friendly string representation."""
        return f"Stack({self._items!r})"
description: A well-written Python Stack class featuring proper type hints, comprehensive docstrings, a custom exception class, clean method structure, and appropriate use of encapsulation. This code should pass a review with no major issues — it represents a best-practice implementation.

name: Empty Input (Edge Case)

name: Non-Code Input — A Poem (Edge Case)
code:
Roses are red,
Violets are blue,
Semicolons are missing,
And so is line two.

The compiler screams,
The runtime weeps,
My stack overflows,
While the deadline creeps.

I debug all night,
By the monitor's glow,
Is it art or code?
The world may never know.
description: A poem about programming submitted as if it were code. Tests whether the agent can recognize that the input is natural language prose rather than source code, and respond appropriately instead of attempting a technical code review.

name: Obfuscated Python One-Liner (Edge Case)
code: print('\n'.join((lambda f: [f(i) for i in range(1, 101)])(lambda x: 'FizzBuzz' if x % 15 == 0 else ('Fizz' if x % 3 == 0 else ('Buzz' if x % 5 == 0 else str(x))))))
description: A valid but heavily obfuscated Python one-liner that implements FizzBuzz using nested lambdas and list comprehensions. Tests the agent's ability to identify readability and maintainability issues in technically correct but intentionally obscure code.
